title: [Quiz] Review the basics of recommender systems.

cues.en: We're not at the point yet where I can turn you loose to start practicing writing your own code for recommender systems, but we will get there soon.
cues.zh: 目前還沒到能讓你自行練習撰寫推薦系統程式碼的階段，不過很快就會到了。

cues.en: Meanwhile, let's do a short quiz to reinforce the things we've talked about so far.
cues.zh: 在那之前，做個簡短測驗，鞏固目前介紹的內容。

cues.en: We talked about the difference between implicit and explicit indications of interest.
cues.zh: 我們談過隱含與明確興趣訊號的差異。

cues.en: Which of these are implicit ratings, as opposed to explicit?
cues.zh: 以下哪些是隱含評分，而不是明確評分？

cues.en: Star reviews, like when you're rating a movie, purchase data, like when you buy something on Amazon, video viewing data, like how many minutes of a YouTube video you watch,
cues.zh: 星級評價，例如替電影評分；購買資料，例如在 Amazon 買東西；影片觀看資料，例如看了 YouTube 影片幾分鐘；

cues.en: and click data, like the record of online ads you've clicked on from an ad network?
cues.zh: 以及點擊資料，例如廣告聯播網記錄你點過的網路廣告？

cues.en: The only example of explicit ratings here is star reviews, where you are explicitly asking a user for their opinion of something.
cues.zh: 這裡唯一的明確評分是星級評價，因為你明確詢問使用者對某件事的意見。

cues.en: Purchasing, viewing, and clicking are all implicit ratings.
cues.zh: 購買、觀看和點擊，都是隱含評分。

cues.en: We can infer you like something because you chose to interact with it somehow.
cues.zh: 因為你選擇以某種方式與它互動，我們便推測你喜歡它。

cues.en: While explicit ratings provide very good data for recommender systems, they require extra work from your users, so it's hard to get enough of them to work with.
cues.zh: 明確評分能為推薦系統提供很好的資料，但需要使用者額外付出心力，因此很難取得足夠的資料。

cues.en: Implicit data, however, is just a byproduct of your users' natural behavior, so it's easy to get lots and lots of it.
cues.zh: 然而，隱含資料只是使用者自然行為的副產品，所以很容易取得大量資料。

cues.en: For a good recommender system, you need both quality and quantity of interest data.
cues.zh: 好的推薦系統，既需要高品質的興趣資料，也需要足夠的數量。

cues.en: Which of the following are examples of recommender systems?
cues.zh: 以下哪些是推薦系統的例子？

cues.en: Some of these are a little tricky, but ask yourself which of these experiences are personalized to your individual past expressions of interest, be they explicit or implicit?
cues.zh: 有些選項有點難，但可以問問自己，哪些體驗會根據你過去明確或隱含表達的個人興趣，進行個人化？

cues.en: We have the movie recommendation widgets you might see on Netflix's home page, the search results you get when using Google, Amazon's people who bought this also bought widget
cues.zh: 選項包括 Netflix 首頁可能看到的電影推薦小工具、使用 Google 得到的搜尋結果、瀏覽商品時 Amazon 顯示的「買過此商品的人也買了」小工具，

cues.en: when you view a product, Pandora's music streaming system, online radio stations where you might be listening to a stream of an over-the-air radio station,
cues.zh: Pandora 的音樂串流系統，以及把無線廣播電台節目放到網路串流播放的線上電台，

cues.en: YouTube, and the search results you get from Wikipedia.
cues.zh: 還有 YouTube，以及 Wikipedia 的搜尋結果。

cues.en: Netflix definitely takes your past viewing and rating behavior into account when recommending things for you to watch, as does YouTube.
cues.zh: Netflix 推薦觀看內容時，確實會考慮你過去的觀看與評分行為，YouTube 也是如此。

cues.en: Your Google search results are personalized based on what Google knows about you, so it too counts as a recommender system, but Wikipedia gives the same search results to everyone,
cues.zh: Google 搜尋結果會根據 Google 對你的了解進行個人化，因此也算推薦系統；但 Wikipedia 給每個人的搜尋結果都一樣，

cues.en: so it's really just an information retrieval system and not a recommender system.
cues.zh: 所以它其實只是資訊檢索系統，而不是推薦系統。

cues.en: We know that Pandora chooses songs for you based on your explicit ratings, so it's a recommender system, but if you listen to your local radio station online, that's not a personalized experience,
cues.zh: 我們知道 Pandora 根據你的明確評分選歌，所以它是推薦系統；但在線上收聽當地廣播電台，並不是個人化體驗，

cues.en: so it doesn't involve recommendation technology.
cues.zh: 因此不涉及推薦技術。

cues.en: Amazon's people who bought also bought also counts as a recommender system, because even though it doesn't involve explicit ratings, it does involve the implicit indication
cues.zh: Amazon 的「買過的人也買了」也算推薦系統，因為儘管不涉及明確評分，卻會用到你

cues.en: of interest you gave to the item this feature appears on, just by viewing it.
cues.zh: 瀏覽出現這項功能的商品時，所提供的隱含興趣訊號。

cues.en: As you can see, there are gray areas here, but the important point is that what you learn about building recommender systems can be applied to a very wide variety of problems in the real world.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，這裡存在灰色地帶，但重點是，建立推薦系統所學的內容，能應用在真實世界各式各樣的問題。

cues.en: And even for the items we didn't select as correct answers, you could imagine building a recommender system for which online radio station you should listen to, and maybe personalizing Wikipedia search
cues.zh: 即使那些沒有選為正確答案的項目，也可以想像建立推薦系統，推薦你該收聽哪個線上電台；而使用推薦系統將 Wikipedia 搜尋

cues.en: with recommender systems isn't so bad of an idea.
cues.zh: 個人化，或許也是個不錯的主意。

cues.en: Which of these are examples of top-N recommender systems, where our aim is just to produce a short list of the best recommendations we can come up with for a given user?
cues.zh: 以下哪些是 Top-N 推薦系統，也就是目標只是為特定使用者，產生一份我們能找到的最佳推薦短清單？

cues.en: Recommendation widgets for Netflix or Amazon generally top out at 20 or so results, and so they qualify as top N recommender systems.
cues.zh: Netflix 或 Amazon 的推薦小工具，通常最多顯示 20 個左右的結果，因此符合 Top-N 推薦系統的定義。

cues.en: Google, however, can return as many results as you would like, so it needs to rank many more pages for you.
cues.zh: 不過，Google 可以傳回你想要的那麼多結果，因此需要為你排序更多網頁。

cues.en: Although, if you restricted Google to only one or two pages of personalized search results, you could also frame it as a top-N recommender.
cues.zh: 當然，如果把 Google 限制為只顯示一兩頁個人化搜尋結果，也可以視為 Top-N 推薦系統。

cues.en: So again, it's a bit of a gray area, but we use the idea of top-N recommenders just to focus our work on what matters, and in the case of top-N, it means we want to focus just on the top results
cues.zh: 所以這裡又有一點灰色地帶，但使用 Top-N 推薦的概念，是為了聚焦在重要的事。對 Top-N 來說，就是只關注每位使用者

cues.en: for each user, and not our ability to predict ratings on everything for everybody.
cues.zh: 最前面的結果，而不是預測每個人對所有東西的評分的能力。

cues.en: Thinking back to our architecture slide for top-N recommender systems, which of the following were boxes in that diagram?
cues.zh: 回想 Top-N 推薦系統的架構投影片，下列哪些是圖中的方塊？

cues.en: Well, candidate shuffling is something I just made up, although we will in fact build recommender systems that just recommend random, shuffled stuff as a baseline to compare against.
cues.zh: 「候選項目隨機重排」是我隨便編出來的。不過，我們確實會建立只推薦隨機打亂項目的系統，作為比較用的基準。

cues.en: Everything else is something we have to do in a top-N recommender.
cues.zh: 其他項目，都是 Top-N 推薦系統必須做的事。

cues.en: We need to generate recommendation candidates based on the user's interests, we need to rank those candidates, and then filter them down to the N results we want.
cues.zh: 我們需要根據使用者興趣產生推薦候選項目、將它們排序，再過濾成所需的 N 個結果。

cues.en: That's it for this quiz and for this initial section of the course.
cues.zh: 這次測驗與課程的第一個章節就到這裡。

cues.en: You've already learned a lot about the concepts, challenges, and architecture of recommender systems.
cues.zh: 你已經學到許多推薦系統的概念、挑戰與架構。

cues.en: Keep on going, as there's a lot more detail and hands-on practice ahead for you.
cues.zh: 繼續吧，前面還有更多細節與實作練習等著你。
